Hi Jared / ACME procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and clear interest from your platform team on latency/cost tradeoffs for inference. As discussed on the call, I wanted to summarize the procurement/commercial questions so we can keep momentum: 

- Primary purchase vehicle: do you prefer PO (net terms) or card? Any internal limits on card transactions?
- Vendor setup: will you use your vendor portal (link below) or an intake packet we return?
- Required forms: W-9 vs W-8 (depending on entity), banking details, tax IDs, insurance certificate (if requested)
- Marketplace: you mentioned possible procurement via AWS Marketplace — is that preferred for speed or do you still need a vendor record?

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a vendor setup packet and our current W-9 + banking stub for your finance team to review (attach after this email).
2) Rishi (cc’d) will follow up on pricing/legal items and can be the point on any SOW/term questions.
3) If you want to run via AWS Marketplace, flag that and we’ll coordinate listing/quoting with our partnerships team.

Attachments I plan to send in the follow-up: vendor_setup_packet.pdf, Redwood_W9_2026.pdf, redwood_banking_info.csv (banking stubs only — no account flow tokens).

If you can confirm PO vs card and whether your portal will accept our packet, I’ll tailor the packet accordingly.

Link to your portal from the demo notes: https://portal.acme-energy.com/vendor-portal/registration/rdw-3321

Thanks — I’ll shoot the packet now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- We prefer PO with net 30 for anything over $10k. Card is OK for pilot/POC transactions under $5k (finance policy).
- We do have a vendor portal (the link you included) and it’s our preferred onboarding path — will need the W-9 and banking stub there.
- We will need a copy of your certificate of insurance before the contract is signed (I’ll open a request ticket).
- AWS Marketplace would be great for ease of billing, but the legal team still requires a vendor record in our portal for SSO/procure checks. We can do both.

I’ve looped procurement@acme-energy.com on next steps below. If you could upload the three documents to our portal, that will speed things up. We typically start vendor intake review within 2 business days of a complete packet.

Thanks — Jared
Jared Lyons
Procurement Lead, ACME Energy
jared.lyons@acme-energy.com
